Būti tokio dydžio, kokio reikia.
To be of the size that is needed.
New shoes fit me.

Drabužiai ir daiktai, kurie dabar patinka žmonėms.
Clothes and things that people now like.
Long skirts have returned to fashion.

Toks, kurį dabar perka ir nešioja jauni žmonės.
One that young people now buy and wear.
The friend has a fashionable jacket.

Lėkštės ir puodukai, kuriuos plauname po valgio.
Plates and cups, which we wash after the meal.
After supper I wash the dishes.

Baltas apvalus indas, ant kurio dedame maistą.
A white round vessel on which we put food.
On the plate lies warm meat.

Iš jo geriame karštą arbatą ar kavą.
From it we drink hot tea or coffee.
Mother pours tea into the cup.

Iš jos geriame šaltą vandenį ar pieną.
From it we drink cold water or milk.
She drinks water from the glass.

Gražus aukštas indas vynui; iš jo geriame per šventes.
A beautiful tall vessel for wine; from it we drink at celebrations.
The guests drink from beautiful wine glasses.

Iš jo pila arbatą į puodukus.
From it tea is poured into cups.
To the guests I carry the teapot and cups.

Aštrus daiktas; juo pjaustome duoną ir mėsą.
A sharp thing; with it we cut bread and meat.
Bread I cut with a sharp knife.

Ja valgome mėsą ir salotas prie stalo.
With it we eat meat and salad at the table.
The child eats meat with a fork.

Juo valgome sriubą ir košę.
With it we eat soup and porridge.
Soup I eat with a big spoon.

Labai mažas daiktas cukrui maišyti arbatoje.
A very small thing for stirring sugar in tea.
She stirs coffee with a teaspoon.

Jame verdame sriubą ant viryklės.
In it we boil soup on the cooker.
The soup boils in a big pot.

Didelis šaukštas sriubai pilti į lėkštes.
A big spoon for pouring soup into plates.
Mother pours soup with the ladle.

Jame vanduo greitai tampa karštas arbatai.
In it water quickly becomes hot for tea.
Turn on the kettle, I want tea.

Joje darome kiaušinienę ant viryklės.
In it we make fried eggs on the cooker.
I make fried eggs in a big frying pan.

Aukštas indas iš stiklo vandeniui ar pienui.
A tall vessel of glass for water or milk.
The child drinks milk from the bottle.

Mažas daiktas; juo atidarome limonado ar alaus butelį.
A small thing; with it we open a lemonade or beer bottle.
Where did you put the bottle opener?

Su juo atidarome vyno butelį per šventę.
With it we open a wine bottle at a celebration.
On the table lies an old corkscrew.

Jame laikome uogienę ar agurkus.
In it we keep jam or cucumbers.
Grandmother opened the jam jar.

Didelis apvalus indas salotoms ar sriubai.
A big round vessel for salad or soup.
Mother puts the salad into the bowl.

Maži mediniai daiktai dėžutėje; su jais kuriame laužą.
Small wooden things in a box; with them we make a bonfire.
Without matches there will be no bonfire.

Graži balta medžiaga po lėkštėmis per šventes.
A beautiful white cloth under the plates at celebrations.
The vase stands on the white tablecloth.

Popierius, kuriuo valome burną po valgio.
A paper with which we clean the mouth after the meal.
The children clean their hands with napkins.

Indas su vandeniu gėlėms ant stalo.
A vessel with water for flowers on the table.
The roses stand in a beautiful vase.

Paprastas daiktas, kuriuo rašome mėlynai ar juodai.
A simple thing with which we write in blue or black.
Sign with a pen, not with a pencil.

Storas daiktas piešti; jo spalvos labai ryškios.
A thick thing for drawing; its colours are very bright.
The children draw with markers.

Brangus ir gražus daiktas, kuriuo pasirašome sutartis.
An expensive and beautiful thing with which we sign contracts.
The director signed the contract with a fountain pen.

Medinis daiktas; juo rašo mokiniai mokykloje.
A wooden thing; with it pupils write at school.
The child holds in the hand a yellow pencil.

Žalia medžio dalis; rudenį jis krenta ant žemės.
A green part of a tree; in autumn it falls to the ground.
The children collect yellow leaves in the park.

Balta medžiaga; su ja vaikai daro paveikslus iš popieriaus.
A white substance; with it children make pictures from paper.
The teacher bought glue and scissors.

Su jais parduotuvėje perkame maistą ir drabužius.
With them at the shop we buy food and clothes.
I do not have money for a ticket.

Tokiais pinigais mokame Lietuvoje ir Latvijoje.
With such money we pay in Lithuania and in Latvia.
The ticket costs one euro.

Mažiausi pinigai; viename eure jų yra šimtas.
The smallest money; in one euro there are a hundred of them.
In the wallet I found a few cents.

Tokiais pinigais moka žmonės Amerikoje.
With such money people pay in America.
The tourist paid with dollars.

Skaičius, kuris rodo dalį nuo šimto.
A number that shows a part out of a hundred.
The bank takes a small percent.

Labai mažas svoris; taip matuojame druską ir cukrų.
A very small weight; thus we measure salt and sugar.
Of salt we put only a few grams.

Juo matuojame mėsos ir sūrio svorį.
With it we measure the weight of meat and cheese.
At the market I bought a kilogram of apples.

Juo matuojame pieną, vandenį ar benziną.
With it we measure milk, water or petrol.
I bought a litre of milk.

Didelis daiktas iš popieriaus ar medžio; į jį dedame knygas.
A big thing of paper or wood; into it we put books.
The books lie in a big box.

Mažas daiktas jogurtui ar grietinei parduotuvėje.
A small thing for yoghurt or cream at the shop.
I bought a container of cream.

Jame parduotuvėje perkame cukrų, druską ar sausainius.
In it at the shop we buy sugar, salt or biscuits.
The child opened the biscuit packet.

Didelis krepšys šiukšlėms ar sunkiems daiktams.
A big bag for rubbish or for heavy things.
The rubbish I put into a big sack.

Mažas indas; jį atidarome pirštu ir geriame limonadą.
A small vessel; we open it with a finger and drink lemonade.
The young man drinks lemonade from the can.

Vieta mieste, kur perkame šviežius vaisius ir sūrį.
A place in the city where we buy fresh fruit and cheese.
On Sunday we go to the market.

Didelė šventė mieste, kur žmonės parduoda savo daiktus.
A big celebration in the city where people sell their things.
At the fair we bought a wooden spoon.

Tai, ką valgome, kai esame alkani.
That which we eat when we are hungry.
At the shop we buy food for the week.
